Theme 066 · Data storytelling

Small Multiples

Edward Tufte's answer to 'compared to what?': a quiet grid of identical little charts sharing one scale, so a single outlier jumps off the page. The film starts in dashboard chaos with 38 mismatched scales, then Acme Pulse snaps everything onto one axis and the broken metric can't hide.

readability ●●●trust ●●●effort low
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

Mismatched tiles fill the grid in a fast diagonal cascade from top-left; sparklines jitter at different scales, and the headline's italic today lands on the downbeat before the drop.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

On the drop 38 tiles collapse to 14 and every sparkline re-scales onto one shared dashed baseline; the centre tile floods teal and the Acme mark pops in on beat 2.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

All 12 sparklines draw left to right in sync; at 09:42 only Checkout conv. breaks downward, its frame turns coral on the snare, then the −18% card and Roll back rise from below.

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

14 small calm charts draw in as a two-row strip; the italic Every minute lands on the downbeat and Start free presses on the last bar.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Multiple tile — hairline frame, identical size and scale — the unit of the whole film
  • Shared baseline — dashed line at 100 % that every tile uses
  • Outlier frame — coral 4 px border + tint for the one tile that breaks
  • Event marker — vertical dashed line at 09:42 inside the tile
  • Mono tile label — 20 px metric name, top-left of every tile
  • Hairline rule — separates the grid from the decision strip

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Grid cascade — tiles fade/scale 0.96 → 1 with a 0.03 s diagonal stagger, power2.out 0.35 s, total one bar at 120 BPM
  • Rescale snap — y-scales tween to the shared domain with expo.inOut 0.5 s landing on the drop
  • Synchronized draw — all sparklines stroke-dashoffset draw together over 4 beats (2 s), outlier breaks on beat 3 with a 0.1 s coral flash

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Identical small charts make the anomaly self-evident without any arrows; it feels like evidence, which is ideal for trust. Risk: a quiet grid can read as a slide — keep the outlier motion bold and let the camera lean in.

Adapt to your product: Put your product's real metrics or entities (services, regions, customers, jobs) into a same-scale grid; your anomaly is the one tile that breaks the pattern.
